identity.description:
Resume an orchestrator after a restart, and close items and runs cleanly

## Summary

An orchestrator can now come back after a compaction, a closed session or a restart of the machine: it reads its record, finds the project leads that still run, joins them again, resumes the conversation of each one that is gone in its own worktree, and arms its usage watch and its GitHub waits again. When an item ends, the orchestrator closes it cleanly: the project lead stops what it started, the session ends and its tab closes, the worktree goes, and the ticket closes. A worktree with changed or untracked files, or with any process still in it, is kept and reported in the inbox, never forced; the orchestrator stops leftover processes only when it can see that the work started them. A close of the whole run does this for each item and marks the record closed as its history. The orchestrator also no longer asks about actions at the start: the allow rules are the authority, and a refused action goes to the inbox.

Closes #156

**Ticket:** [#156 — crew:orchestrator: resume after a restart, and the close-out](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/156)
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.145 (new): the decisions of this change and their reasons. §15.140 (launcher), §15.142 (skill), §15.143 (board) for the parts it builds on.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/resume-and-close.md` (new) owns the resume, the close of an item and the close of a run.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns `start`, `resume`, `find`, `stop` and `remove`, their output and exit codes.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md` owns `closed_at`, `close` and `launch.session_id`.
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md` owns "The authority" and points at the reference above.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/references/resume-and-close.md`: new. The three resume cases (compaction, reopened session, new session), the seven resume steps, the four close steps of an item and their order, the close of a run, and how crew works beside the `cc-restore` plugin.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py`: `start` passes `claude --session-id <uuid>` and prints a tenth field `session_id`. New `resume` opens a tab in an existing worktree with `claude --resume <id>`, with the same model, settings and one-tab guarantees as `start`; with no id it takes the newest transcript of the worktree; exit 8 when the session is already open. New `find` prints the handle of each tab or pane whose `claude` process has `--name <name>` (match `name`), the record's session id after `--resume` or `--session-id` (match `id`), or its cwd in the worktree (match `cwd`). New `remove` refuses with exit 9 and no change on changed or untracked files or on any process in the worktree, and lists each one; with `--stop-processes` it stops each process with no terminal and names it, signals a pid only when a fresh `ps` and `lsof` read shows the same argv and cwd, scans the worktree again after the stop and refuses while any process is still there, and still refuses on a process with a terminal or on its own cwd or an ancestor's; it deletes the branch only with `--delete-branch`, and keeps it, with its commits listed in `branch_only_commits`, when it holds a commit that no other branch, remote-tracking ref or tag holds. A failed `lsof` exits 6. `stop` sends Escape and Ctrl-U, then `/exit`, before it closes the tab; with `--name` or `--session-id` it acts only when a `claude` on the handle's tty matches by name or id, because a new tmux server reuses pane ids.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: checks for all of the above, with stub `ps` and `lsof`. 185 checks.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md`: documents the new subcommands, the tenth field, exit codes 8 and 9, and what `remove` does with a person's shell or editor.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-orch.py`: `closed_at` (null from `init`, null for an old record), the `close` command, and `session_id` in `LAUNCH_KEYS`.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh`: checks for `close`, a second `close`, an old record, and `launch.session_id`.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md`: `closed_at`, ten `launch` keys, "Closing the record".
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md`: points at the new reference for the compaction, the resume and the close; a trigger for "resume orchestrator <name>"; "The authority at the start" becomes "The authority", with no ask and a notice for a refused action; the goal message rule "Uncovered actions" becomes "A refused action"; `--ticket-url` at `item add` and `group add`.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`: the new reference, the launcher's new subcommands, the build state, and how a person resumes or closes a run.
- `docs/design.md`: §15.145; §15.140 now says that the Remote Control default held on real sessions; §15.143 says 29 tests.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: 0.1.112.

### Constraints that applied

- One owner per rule: each command's arguments, output and exit codes stay in `launcher.md` or `orchestrator-record.md`; the reference names the command and points there.
- No test starts a real `claude`: `test-launcher.sh` uses `CREW_LAUNCHER_CLAUDE` and stubs for `tmux`, `osascript`, `uv`, `ps` and `lsof`.
- Issue 150 rules 15 and 16: `resume` passes `--model` (default `opus`) and the one merged `--settings` with `"remoteControlAtStartup": false`.
- `remove` ends no process by default and none silently, never ends its caller or a process above it, keeps a person's shell or editor, and has no force flag.
- `find` matches exactly: a token pair or an equal cwd, never a substring and never a tab title, which Claude Code decorates.
- Version 0.1.112 and §15.145 come from the orchestrator.

### How this was verified

- `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: 185 of 185 checks passed, on `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6.
- `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh`: all checks passed, on `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6, after the rebase on the board and Python 3.9 PRs.
- A probe: one `claude` in a tmux pane with no setting sources and a `SessionEnd` hook in `--settings`. `/exit` gave the reason `prompt_input_exit`. That is the reason on which `cc-restore` forgets a session.
- `ps` on a live session: a process that Claude Code's Bash tool starts in the background has no controlling terminal, and the `claude` process has the tab's tty.
- `osascript` on live iTerm2 sessions: session names read as "✳ orch-record (claude)", so `find` does not use them.
- A skeptical review of the local head before the first push: 2 blocking, 4 suggestions, 2 nits, 1 unsure. Fixed all: `remove` no longer stops a process by default, because a GUI editor started with `code .` looks the same as a left-behind server; `stop` clears an open permission dialog before `/exit`; the rejoin message no longer duplicates live watches; a run close marks unmerged items `closed`; `lsof` failure is an error; a session that `cc-restore` resumed is restarted by the launcher; `find` accepts an npm `claude`; a stale line and long lines. Round 2 (on `remove` and `stop`, after the CI review's five findings were fixed): 1 blocking, 2 suggestions, all fixed: `stop` checks its target, `remove` scans again after the stop, and a match by cwd alone is never stopped. The round 2 fixes had no third local round; the CI review reads them.

### Known gaps

- No orchestrator has resumed or closed an item with these scripts yet. The orchestrator of this build plans to run the close-out on its idle implementers.
- The tests do not prove how Claude Code's input box takes Escape, Ctrl-U, then `/exit` and Enter. The probe proved only `/exit` and Enter on tmux.
- `remove` finds a process by its cwd only. A container or a server that runs from another directory is the project lead's to stop, at close step 1.
